biothings.name: resistant hypertension
biothings.definition: A severe medical condition which is estimated to appear in 9-18% of hypertensive patients, in which treatment with 3 or more antihypertensive drugs including diuretics are ineffective. [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6195-6976, PMID:26935512]

biothings.name: malignant essential hypertension
biothings.definition: Essential hypertension with rapid progression to severe high blood pressure, papilledema, and renal failure. [NCIT:P378]
biothings.synonyms: accelerated essential hypertension, malignant essential hypertension

biothings.name: essential hypertension
biothings.definition: Hypertension that presents without an identifiable cause. [NCIT:P378]

biothings.name: renovascular hypertension
biothings.definition: High blood pressure secondary to renal artery stenosis. [NCIT:P378]

biothings.name: essential hypertension, genetic
biothings.definition: An instance of essential hypertension that is caused by a modification of the individual's genome. [MONDO:patterns/genetic]
biothings.synonyms: blood pressure regulation QTL, genetic essential hypertension, hypertension, essential, salt-sensitive

opentargets.name: hypertensive disorder
opentargets.description: Persistently high systemic arterial blood pressure. Based on multiple readings (blood pressure determination), hypertension is currently defined as when systolic pressure is consistently greater than 140 mm Hg or when diastolic pressure is consistently 90 mm Hg or more.

opentargets.name: pulmonary arterial hypertension
opentargets.description: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a group of diseases characterized by mean pulmonary artery pressure >20 mmHg and elevated pulmonary arterial resistance leading to right heart failure. PAH is progressive and potentially fatal. PAH may be idiopathic and/ or familial, have overt features of venous/capillary involvement (pulmonary veno-occlusive disease, PVOD/pulmonary capillary hemangiomatosis, PCH), induced by drug or toxin (drug-or toxin-induced PAH), or associated with other diseases like congenital heart disease, connective tissue disease, HIV, schistosomiasis, portal hypertension (PAH associated with other disease).

opentargets.name: essential hypertension, genetic
opentargets.description: An instance of essential hypertension that is caused by a modification of the individual's genome.

opentargets.name: essential hypertension
opentargets.description: Hypertension that presents without an identifiable cause.

opentargets.name: Pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with portal hypertension
opentargets.description: Pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with portal hypertension (PAH-PH) is a form of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), characterized by an elevated pulmonary arterial resistance leading to right heart failure observed as a complication of portal hypertension.
